Brief: Tell me about the Rosetta mission and what it found at comet 67P. — about Discovery

1. Churyumov–Gerasimenko was discovered in 1969 by Klim Ivanovich Churyumov of Kyiv University's Astronomical Observatory, who examined a photograph that had been exposed for comet Comas Solà by Svetlana Ivanovna Gerasimenko on 11 September 1969 at the Alma-Ata Astrophysical Institute, near Alma-Ata, the then-capital city of Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic, Soviet Union.
2. Churyumov found a cometary object near the edge of the plate, but assumed that this was comet Comas Solà.
3. After returning to his home institute in Kyiv, Churyumov examined all the photographic plates more closely.
